parsed.why: No trans criminalisation, but frequent government crackdowns on visible LGBTQ presence, police closure of venues and pride, zero discrimination protection, and a 69% poll backing criminalisation — documented hostility with thin recourse.

Strong constitutional and high-court protections, decriminalisation and working relief (passport exam case), offset by documented airport stops, railway police groping under gender-check pretext, degrading custody, and removal of trans-specific sexual-violence offences.

Hate-crime law, X passport markers, preference-based custody resolution and enforced business anti-discrimination are strong positives; offset by a state prison census showing trans women in male units, drink-spiking robbery patterns, and threats against trans candidates.

Self-ID recognition, identity-based facility access, enforced transphobia aggravation with real sentences, and official tourism welcoming; one region's repeal of non-discrimination and conversion-therapy rules plus conservative areas outside cities holds it below the top tier.

Total civil-society repression leaving no space for LGBT life, official denial and slur-based hostility, undefined discretionary morality provisions, no recourse or community infrastructure, and defector-documented executions — structural facts imply catastrophic exposure if outed.
